_note: How requirement wording maps onto the bench (v2.14). A trigger phrase names the bench fault that puts it into effect; a reaction phrase names the state the oracle checks. The rules drafter only accepts a requirement whose trigger and reaction are both listed here; anything else is 'unparsed' and needs a hand-written basis in design/basis/<req>.json (or, later, an LLM draft) that passes the same checks.

triggers._cause_note: when the link comes back, the first frame after the gap fails the sequence check, so E2E_INVALID can win the race against the timeout (bench finding 2)

persistence._note: v2.35: '... stop if it persists >= N ms' (SR-07 to SR-09). The controller judges a breach once per command frame, so it stops at the first breached frame that is N ms or more after the first one (config safety.env_debounce_ms). Code owns the durations of the cases; the model never sets them.
persistence._smoothed_note: Measured on the reference (v2.35): accel_req follows the model exactly (a 61 ms injection stops, 60 ms does not). steer_rate and speed_req go through the planner's own smoothing, so the breach outlives the injection: speed_req stops already at 20 ms, steer_rate stays NORMAL at 20 ms and stops at 30 ms. The fault duration is not the breach duration, and the 50 ms boundary cannot be set through them.

start_speeds_note: EP over the start speed: low, mid and just inside the ODD limit (from the config)
